svg.title: Projects and shared shell V1
svg.desc: Proposed Projects layouts at 1440, 880 and 320 CSS pixels, transition into the workbench and representative feedback states.
svg.text: PROPOSAL · 15 November 2026 · static source-informed wireframes; no implementation or usability claim
Desktop · 1440 CSS px · project list first; create and restore alongside
Applied work is retained automatically in this browser profile.
Keep independent backups: browser storage can be cleared or become unavailable.
Applied work is retained automatically in this browser profile.
Keep independent backups: browser storage can be cleared or become unavailable.
Names can repeat. Exact identities distinguish these two projects.
Normal page scroll reveals longer lists and feedback.
storage can be cleared or become
Same reading order at all widths.
Content scrolls; no fixed action bar.
Applied work is retained in this browser.
Select a token to inspect it.
Open uses the existing project ID.
Projects invokes the existing departure guard.
Keep editing preserves the draft; confirmed
Resize/Back rules remain in shell V1.
No projects retained in this browser.
Use New project or Restore backup below.
Status replaces the list, never fake rows.
Create and Restore stay disabled until read.
Show the actual error as an alert.
Retained result unknown. Entered name is
Keep the entered name, actual error/notice
This is not a failed-create retry.
Shared: header geometry, semantic theme, flexible region, modal/focus conventions.
Projects: catalogue → New project → Restore backup → recovery/error/notice.
App + useProjects retain host/entry authority; Workbench retains command authority.
Shared presentational shell is a candidate extraction, not a new controller.
No selection step, project inspector, cloud account, search or invented dates.
Sample names, counts, UUIDs and unsupported-version reason are illustrative. All identity text must wrap exactly without truncation.
Retained-but-unreadable and pending states keep their existing recovery controls; restore still opens its protected review dialog.
Static forms are shown for hierarchy only. Accessible errors, keyboard/focus, control fit and short-height scrolling need later runtime verification.
